accepted.question_text: Determine how a finite subtraction set controls the length and structure of the resulting nim-sequence period, extend that analysis to partizan subtraction games with separate subtraction sets for the two players, and resolve the related open questions about complete analysis of three-member subtraction sets, superpolynomial versus polynomial period growth, characterization of purely periodic subtraction sets, and periodicity behavior for infinite subtraction games and aperiodic subtraction/division variants.

evidence.quote: Subtraction games with finite subtraction sets are known to have periodic nim-sequences. Investigate the relationship between the subtraction set and the length and structure of the period. The same question can be asked about partizan subtraction games ... It would now seem feasible to give the complete analysis for games whose subtraction sets have just three members ... It would also be of interest to characterize the subtraction sets which yield a purely periodic nim-sequence ... For infinite subtraction games in general there are corresponding questions about the length and purity of the period.

accepted.question_text: Decide whether every finite octal game is ultimately periodic, resolve the many listed outstanding octal codes and related splitting games such as Treblecross and Couples-Are-Forever, determine whether large nim-values such as 2048 occur in Treblecross, explain the structure of periods in those octal games already known to be periodic, and clarify the computational complexity of octal, partizan octal, and related poset-style heap games.

evidence.quote: Are all finite octal games ultimately periodic? ... Resolve any number of outstanding particular cases ... Perhaps the most notorious and deserving of attention is the game ·007 ... Will 2048 ever be reached? ... Explain the structure of the periods of games known to be periodic.

accepted.question_text: Complete the analysis of unsolved hexadecimal heap games by establishing periodicity or arithmetic periodicity where suspected, and resolve the explicitly listed outstanding hexadecimal codes whose full behavior remains unknown.

evidence.quote: Such games may be arithmetically periodic ... The game ·9 has not so far yielded its complete analysis ... Other unsolved hexadecimal games are ...

accepted.question_text: For N-heap Wythoff Game with N at least 3, prove or disprove Fraenkel’s two conjectures describing the eventual structure of P-positions when N−2 heaps are fixed, including the mex-plus-shift description and the eventual golden-ratio asymptotic formula.

evidence.quote: For N ≥ 3, Fraenkel makes the following conjectures. Conjecture 1 ... Conjecture 2 ...

accepted.question_text: Determine the actual game values in End-Nim, analyze impartial and partizan End-Wythoff and Fraenkel’s generalized end-heap Wythoff variant, analyze Hub-and-Spoke Nim and the natural forest generalization, and decide how broadly integer-valued behavior fails or holds in Red-Blue Cherries positions.

evidence.quote: Wolfe asks for the actual values. Nowakowski suggested to analyze impartial and partizan END-WYTHOFF ... Fraenkel asks a similar question ... There is also HUB-AND-SPOKE NIM ... The most natural variant is that beans may only be taken from a leaf ... They ask this: Is every RED-BLUE CHERRIES position an integer?

accepted.question_text: Extend the analysis of Kotzig’s Nim by deciding whether every finite move set yields eventual periodicity as the circle length grows, analyzing the misère version, and resolving the stated conjectures for specific move sets such as {1,4} and {3,5}.

evidence.quote: Extend the analysis of KOTZIG’S NIM. Is the game eventually periodic in terms of the length of the circle for every finite move set? Analyze the misère version of KOTZIG’S NIM.

accepted.question_text: Obtain asymptotic estimates for the proportions of N-, O-, and P-positions in Epstein’s Put-or-Take-a-Square game.

evidence.quote: Obtain asymptotic estimates for the proportions of N-, O- and P-positions in Epstein’s PUT-OR-TAKE-A-SQUARE game.

accepted.question_text: Analyze the still-open four-heap case of Gale’s Nim when all heap sizes are distinct and greater than 2, and extend the analysis to the natural generalization with h heaps where play ends once k heaps have vanished.

evidence.quote: GALE’S NIM ... the situation where the four heaps have distinct sizes greater than 2 is open. An obvious generalization is to play with h heaps and play finishes when k of them have vanished.

accepted.question_text: Extend the known analysis of Euclid’s Nim from two integers to broader settings, including the partially solved three-integer case, and determine values or at least atomic weights for Partizan Euclid positions.

evidence.quote: Collins and Lengyel play EUCLID’S NIM with three integers and solve some special cases. In PARTIZAN EUCLID ... Determining the values seems hard. The atomic weights may be easier.

accepted.question_text: Complete the odd-parameter analysis of Dudeney, explain the evidence suggesting arbitrarily long pearl-string periods and possibly incompletable behavior, and determine the structure underlying the unresolved odd-Y cases.

evidence.quote: If Y is even, the analysis is easy. Some advance in the analysis, when Y is odd, has been made ... It seems likely ... But there is some evidence to suggest that an analysis will never be complete ... Moreover, the periods of the pearl-strings appear to become arbitrarily long.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether Schuhstrings can have arbitrarily many simultaneous string terminations, extending the known example with three simultaneous terminations.

evidence.quote: Kevin Saff has found three such strings ... and he conjectures that there can be arbitrarily many such simultaneous terminations.

accepted.question_text: Analyze DUDE, the unbounded Dudeney game, and explain the apparent lack of a simple pattern in its nim-values.

evidence.quote: Analyze DUDE, i.e., unbounded DUDENEY ... The nim-values do not seem to show an easily described pattern.

accepted.question_text: Develop fuller analyses of games with pass moves, including complete or improved solutions for Nim with a pass, Chocolate Bar with a pass when s is even, regularity questions for octal games with a pass, the case of more than one pass, and structural questions about Oslo versions of games.

evidence.quote: NIM WITH PASS ... obtaining a full solution may be intractable ... CHOCOLATE BAR with a pass ... ask for a solution when s is even. In octal games, with a single pass ... ask for the regularities that can occur in the G-sequences. Now what happens if more than one pass is allowed?

accepted.question_text: Analyze the still-open games with a Muller twist proposed in the literature, solve Blocking Nim with blocks on two heaps, all three heaps, or more than three heaps, and determine the behavior of complementary subtraction games for Fibonacci, modular, and Wythoff-type subtraction sets.

evidence.quote: Smith and Stanic̆a ... propose several other such games which are still open ... ask for an analysis of this game with a block on just two heaps, or on all three. There are corresponding questions for games with more than three heaps ... We ask what happens in this game if S = {an : n + 1, 2, 3, . . .}.

accepted.question_text: Advance misère analysis of octal and quaternary games by deciding whether the Dawson’s Kayles quotient becomes infinite at heap 34, producing presentations and detection algorithms for infinite misère quotients, and defining and detecting algebraic periodicity well enough to solve the listed periodic octal examples.

evidence.quote: The misère quotient of ·07 ... has order 638 at heap size 33. Is it infinite at heap size 34? ... Given a set of games A, describe an algorithm to determine whether the misère quotient of A is infinite ... Give complete misère analyses for any of the ... octal games that show “algebraic-periodicity” in misère play. Give a precise definition of algebraic periodicity and describe an algorithm for detecting and generalizing it.

accepted.question_text: Prove or refute the conjecture that every MNEM position has finite nim-value, and prove or refute the claimed formula that in MEM and MNEM one has value floor(n/k) whenever k squared is at least n.

evidence.quote: They conjecture this: Every position in MNEM has finite nim value ... They also conjecture the following: For both MEM and MNEM, if k^2 ≥ n, then (n, k) = bn/kc.

accepted.question_text: Extend Fibonacci Nim beyond the solved cases by analyzing the multiheap game for values of α other than 2 and for larger numbers of heaps.

evidence.quote: For two heaps, they characterize the P-positions ... The cases for different α and for more heaps are open.

accepted.question_text: Extend the analysis of self-referential subtraction games by solving SUSEN for more than three heaps and solving the still-unsolved two-heap case of ALBUS.

evidence.quote: Alex Fink gives a proof that (a, b, c) is in P ... Extend the analysis to more heaps. ... In ALBUS ... The case of two heaps is still unsolved.

accepted.question_text: Resolve the specific ko-temperature problem at N4 in the Jiang–Rui position, and more broadly unify or sharply distinguish atomic weight theory from Nakamura’s liberty theory while extending liberty theory to practical Go complications such as internal and external kos.

evidence.quote: At move 85, Black takes the ko at L6. What then is the temperature at N4? ... Either find a common formulation which includes much or all of atomic weight theory and Nakamura’s theory of liberties, or find some significant differences. Important practical applied problem: Extend Nakamura’s theory to include other complications which often arise in GO, such as simple kos, either internal and/or external.

accepted.question_text: Extend current analyses of Woodpush from three-piece positions to positions with more pieces and understand draw behavior under superko.

evidence.quote: use top-down thermography to analyze the three-piece positions. What about more pieces? ... show that ... are draws by superko.

accepted.question_text: Make progress on Elkies’s conjecture that values ∗k occur for all k in sufficiently large pawn endings, analyze Impartial Chess, and determine larger transfinite or multidimensional values in Infinite Chess and 3-dimensional Chess.

evidence.quote: He would still welcome progress with his conjecture that the value ∗k occurs for all k ... Thea van Roode has suggested IMPARTIAL CHESS ... They ask about 3-dimensional CHESS.

accepted.question_text: Improve the king-and-rook versus king analysis and determine whether the boiling point of Entrepreneurial Chess is 55/8.

evidence.quote: Low and Stamp have given a strategy ... Berlekamp and Low conjecture that the boiling point of ECHESS is 55/8.

accepted.question_text: Determine the nim-values of the nonattacking queens game on boards larger than size 10.

evidence.quote: They give nim-values for boards of sizes 1 ≤ n ≤ 10 ... and ask for the values of larger boards.

accepted.question_text: Determine the outcome of the 6×6 game of Amazons.

evidence.quote: Müller has shown that the 5×5 game is a first player win and asks about the 6 × 6 game.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether natural stopper positions with wild cycles exist in Phutball-like games, whether noncollusive draws or P-positions occur in standard Phutball, analyze PHLAG Phutball boards, and give a complete analysis of 2×n Directional Phutball.

evidence.quote: Aaron Siegel asks if there are positions ... which are stoppers but contain a wild cycle ... it is not clear if they occur without collusion of the players ... raises the question of whether there is any P-position ... She asks for a complete analysis of the 2 × n board.

accepted.question_text: Quantify first-player winning efficiency in Hex by finding the shortest guaranteed winning path on an n×n board and the minimum number of moves that guarantees a first-player win.

evidence.quote: For each n, what is the shortest path on an n × n board with which the first player can guarantee a win? (2) What is the least number of moves that guarantees the first player a win?

accepted.question_text: Formalize and prove the listed large-board escape, critical-rank, retreat-rule, and board-width/board-count assertions for Fox and Geese, including the explicit thesis conjectures for special n×4, n×6, and Ceylonese-rule positions.

evidence.quote: the following open problems are given: (1) Define a position’s span ... (2) Show that any formation of three Geese ... (3) Welton asks what happens if the Fox is empowered to retreat ... (4) What happens if the number of Geese and board widths are changed? ... In Aaron Siegel’s thesis there are several other questions ...

accepted.question_text: Decide whether the displayed sequences of Hare and Hounds positions become increasingly hot or have arbitrarily large negative atomic weight, and prove or disprove the explicit value conjecture for the starting position on a 6n+5 by 3 board.

evidence.quote: Aaron Siegel asks if the sequences of positions ... are increasingly hot ... if they have arbitrarily large negative atomic weight. He also conjectures that the starting position on a 6n + 5 × 3 board ... has value ...

accepted.question_text: Extend Domineering analysis by resolving open rectangular-board values, especially on 2×n, 3×n, and 4×n boards, characterizing hot positions up to infinitesimal shift, finding new temperatures, and pushing the partial analysis of Tromineering.

evidence.quote: DOMINEERING ... Extend the analysis ... the value of a 2 × n board, for n even, is only known to within “ish”, and that there are problems on 3 × n and 4 × n boards that are still open. Berlekamp asks ... to characterize all hot DOMINEERING positions ... asks for a DOMINEERING position with a new temperature ... Blanco and Fraenkel have obtained partial results for the game of TROMINEERING.

accepted.question_text: Determine the nim-dimension of one-dimensional and two-dimensional NoGo, and decide whether there is a bound on the denominators of fractions that occur on the two-dimensional board.

evidence.quote: We ask for the nim-dimension of both the one- and two-dimensional board. Is there a limit to the denominator of the fractions found on the two-dimensional board?

accepted.question_text: Resolve the listed narrow-board Dots-and-Boxes conjectures, including the Faroese and Icelandic one-dimensional cases, eventual periodicity in misère Swedish 1×n Dots-and-Boxes, and a complete impartial theory for the Icelandic 1×n game.

evidence.quote: For the Faroese, they also conjecture ... Sierra also conjectures for Icelandic DOTS-AND-BOXES ... They also conjecture that the outcome of misère 1×n Swedish DOTS-AND-BOXES is eventually periodic ... Elwyn Berlekamp asks for a complete theory of the impartial Icelandic 1 × n game.

accepted.question_text: Extend the analysis of Sprouts in either normal or misère play.

evidence.quote: SPROUTS. Extend the analysis of this Conway–Paterson game in either the normal or misère form.

accepted.question_text: Extend the analysis of Sylver Coinage.

evidence.quote: SYLVER COINAGE ... Extend the analysis.

accepted.question_text: Extend the analysis of Von Neumann’s Game from directed forests to directed acyclic graphs.

evidence.quote: Extend Úlehla’s or Berlekamp’s analysis of VON NEUMANN’S GAME from directed forests to directed acyclic graphs.

accepted.question_text: Push further analysis of Inverting Hackenbush and Reversing Hackenbush.

evidence.quote: there is plenty of room for further analysis of both games.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether Beanstalk has any O-positions, meaning positions of infinite remoteness.

evidence.quote: We still don’t know if there are any O-positions (positions of infinite remoteness).

accepted.question_text: Prove or disprove the conjecture that for a at least d at least 3 and all sufficiently large n the Erdős–Szekeres Sequence Game is a first-player win in normal and misère play, extend the rational-number variant, and analyze the permutation-graph variant.

evidence.quote: They conjecture that for a ≥ d ≥ 3 and all sufficiently large n, it is N with both normal and misère play, and also with normal play when played with the rationals ... They also suggest investigating the form of the game in which players take turns naming pairs (i, πi) ...

accepted.question_text: Extend the analysis of Thinning Thickets from very thin trees to general trees.

evidence.quote: They ask to extend the analysis to general trees.

accepted.question_text: Extend the analysis of Chomp by solving the infinite three-dimensional game, proving or disproving uniqueness of the winning move from a 3×n rectangle, computing the nim-value of transfinite Chomp position ω×4, and resolving the transfinite stratification conjecture.

evidence.quote: David Gale asks for the solution of the infinite 3D version ... Is there a deterministic proof that there is a unique winning move from a 3×n rectangle? ... An open question is to calculate the nim-value of the position ω×4 ... Perhaps the most fascinating open question ... is their stratification conjecture.

accepted.question_text: Determine the remaining structure of (n;k) Subset Take-Away after the original broad conjectures were disproved.

evidence.quote: Counterexamples to conjectures about subset takeaway ... these are false ... The second player wins (7; 3), but 4 does not divide 7.

accepted.question_text: Make substantial progress on sowing or Mancala games, which the paper identifies as a still-fruitful and largely untouched field of investigation.

evidence.quote: There appears to have been no advance ... although we feel that this should be a fruitful field of investigation at several different levels.

accepted.question_text: Decide whether there is a polynomial-time algorithm for k-Annihilation when k is greater than 1.

evidence.quote: Fraenkel asks: Is there a polynomial algorithm for k > 1?

accepted.question_text: Decide whether palindromic positions in Toppling Dominoes have uniquely occurring values, determine actual values in Timber and Partizan Timber more systematically, and characterize whether some values never occur in the partizan setting.

evidence.quote: Several conjectures are listed but the most intriguing seems to be this: If G is a palindrome then G’s value appears uniquely. ... Values, however, appear to be difficult to determine. ... In the other direction, are there any values that do not occur in the game?

accepted.question_text: Find second-player-win scoring variations of two-player Tower of Hanoi if any exist, and extend the still-incomplete analysis of Hanoi Stick-Up beyond the cases already solved.

evidence.quote: Almost all are first-player wins. Are there any variations with second-player wins? ... They also found the normal and misère outcomes of all positions with up to six stacks, but there is more to be discovered.

accepted.question_text: Decide whether full-deck Beggar-My-Neighbor has any draws or cycles.

evidence.quote: Are there any draws in BEGGAR-MY-NEIGHBOR? ... the problem for the whole deck ... is still open.

accepted.question_text: Construct a game with simple playable rules, finitely many options per move, a simple explicit strategy, play length at most exponential in the input, and NP-hard-or-harder decision complexity.

evidence.quote: So we are led to the following reformulation of Berlekamp’s question: Is there a game which has 1. simple, playable rules, 2. a finite set of options at every move, 3. a simple explicit strategy, 4. length of play at most exponential, and 5. is NP-hard or harder.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether there exist partizan games G1, G2, and G3 such that each component, each adjacent sum, and all their options have polynomial-time strategies, while the sum G1+G3 is NP-hard.

evidence.quote: Aviezri Fraenkel asks: Are there partizan games G1, G2, G3 such that ... G1 + G3 is NP-hard?

accepted.question_text: Determine whether the winner of a sum of switch games of the form a k b | c or a | b k c can be decided in polynomial time or is NP-hard.

evidence.quote: Is there a polynomial time algorithm to determine who wins in G, or is the problem NP-hard?

accepted.question_text: Give formal and algorithmic foundations for sentestrat and top-down thermography, compute or characterize dogmatic thermographs of double kos, build a temperature theory for all loopy games, and characterize natural conditions under which the overheating homomorphism is uniquely determined.

evidence.quote: would like to see a formal proof that sentestrat works, an algorithm for top-down thermography ... Develop the machinery for computing dogmatic thermographs of double kos ... Develop a temperature theory that applies to all loopy games ... asks for a natural set of conditions under which the mapping G ↦ *G is the unique homomorphism that annihilates all infinitesimals.

accepted.question_text: Find a notion of simplest form that works for all finite loopy games including Carousel, detect natural wild cycles in playable games such as Phutball, and characterize when infinitesimal stoppers have well-defined atomic weight together with an algorithm to compute it.

evidence.quote: Is there an alternative notion of simplest form that works for all finite loopy games, and, in particular, for the CAROUSEL? ... the question is to detect one “in nature” ... Siegel also asks under what conditions does a given infinitesimal have a well-defined atomic weight, and asks to specify an algorithm to calculate the atomic weight of an infinitesimal stopper g.

accepted.question_text: Characterize where the nimber ∗2 can occur in natural games and, more generally, determine the smallest exponent bound controlling which nimbers ∗k can appear in a given game.

evidence.quote: Elwyn Berlekamp asks for the habitat of ∗2 ... Given a game, let n be the smallest nonnegative integer n such that if a position of the game has value ∗k then k < 2^n.

accepted.question_text: Tighten the growth bounds for numbers of games born by day n, determine structural properties of games born by day 3 and of alternative birthday partial orders, describe the exact structure and parameters of the lattices L3 and L4, characterize which seed sets generate distributive or modular lattices, understand handedness in all-small lattices, count option-closed games, and find other natural planar lattice families.

evidence.quote: asks us to tighten these bounds ... asks what group is generated by the all-small games ... Describe the partial order of games born by day 3 ... What is the structure of the partial order given by one of these alternative definitions of birthday? ... They ask for a description of the exact structure of L3 ... suggests that it may be possible to find its dimension and the maximum longitude ... They ask which sets of games will give a distributive lattice? Is there a set which will give a nondistributive but modular lattice? ... Do the elements of L0_n have an intrinsic “handedness” ... the question of how many? remains unanswered. Are there other natural families of games that form planar lattices?

accepted.question_text: Given a group or monoid of games, develop a general method for calculating the simplest game in each equivalence class modulo that structure.

evidence.quote: specify a technique for calculating the simplest game in each K-equivalence class.

accepted.question_text: Integrate search methods with a canonical-form engine for combinatorial games.

evidence.quote: would like to investigate how search methods might be integrated with a canonical-form engine.

accepted.question_text: Develop a misère theory for unions of partizan games.

evidence.quote: Develop a misère theory for unions of partizan games.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether there is a useful general theory for games with four outcomes—Next, Previous, Left, and Right—beyond the usual impartial normal-play and misère frameworks.

evidence.quote: Is there a class of games in which there are four outcomes, Next, Previous, Left and Right, and for which a general theory can be given?

accepted.question_text: Resolve the open structural questions about impartial misère quotients, including faithfulness of quotient maps, subgroup intersections with P, classification growth, existence of quotient elements of specific periods such as 5 or 8, and smallest quotients containing specified periods.

evidence.quote: (1) A quotient map ... is said to be faithful ... Is every quotient map faithful? ... Must S ∩ P be nonempty? ... Extend the classification of impartial misère quotients ... Exhibit an impartial misère quotient with a period-5 element ... What is the smallest quotient containing a period 4 (or 3 or 6) element?

accepted.question_text: Characterize inverses in partizan misère universes by determining when G plus its conjugate is equivalent to zero in dicotic settings, whether every inverse must be the conjugate in suitably closed universes, and which universes forbid nonconjugate inverses.

evidence.quote: Allen asks, in the dicotic universe D, when is it true that G+G ≡0 (mod D)? ... if G + H ≡ 0 (mod U), is it necessarily true that H = G? ... in what universes U do we have no nonconjugate inverses?

accepted.question_text: Determine whether guaranteed scoring games are the largest conjugation- and disjunctive-sum-closed scoring universe into which normal-play games order-embed, and solve the game of Brushes.

evidence.quote: They ask: Is the set of guaranteed scoring games the largest subset of scoring games ... in which normal play games can be order-embedded? ... They ask for a solution of BRUSHES.

accepted.question_text: Find a formula for the number of P-positions of Nim with 2n tokens and, more generally, develop methods to enumerate P-positions of a given size for arbitrary games.

evidence.quote: Find a formula for the number of P-positions for NIM played with 2n tokens ... In general, given a game, enumerate the number of P-positions of a given size.

accepted.question_text: For square-free lattice games and related lattice-point rulesets, determine whether winning moves from any N-position can be computed efficiently.

evidence.quote: Miller and Guo conjecture that there are efficient algorithms for determining the winning moves from any N-position.

accepted.question_text: Determine the nim-dimension of specific natural games and better understand the range of possible nim-dimensions across games such as Domineering and Amazons.

evidence.quote: One can ask for the nim-dimension for each game one encounters ... it is conjectured that DOMINEERING ... has nim-dimension = 1 ... and AMAZONS ... has nim-dimension 2.

accepted.question_text: Decide whether every game with bounded nim-dimension has only finitely many exceptional cases in its atomic-weight calculations.

evidence.quote: They ask if this is true for any game with bounded nim-dimension.

accepted.question_text: Find other universal partizan games besides Generalized Konane, and develop general techniques for proving that certain game values cannot occur in a given ruleset.

evidence.quote: Are there any other universal games? ... A related question: are there any general techniques that, given a game, show that certain values do not occur?

accepted.question_text: Determine boiling points of specific rulesets such as Domineering and develop feasible methods for obtaining strong upper bounds on temperatures.

evidence.quote: It is conjectured that the boiling point of DOMINEERING ... is 2. Find feasible methods that give good upper bounds on the temperatures.

accepted.question_text: Develop a clearer theory of joins of games, including compatibility and switching mechanisms among normal, misère, and nearly disjunctive compositions.

evidence.quote: The two games must be compatible in some not-well-defined sense ... makes it an option for a player to switch games ... introduced WHIM ... explore another possible join.

accepted.question_text: Analyze multiplayer game behavior under different preference systems, especially the remaining open cases of misère three-player Nim and broader recursive/canonical-form questions for cooperative multiplayer sums.

evidence.quote: If a player cannot win but can make either of the other two the winner, how should play proceed? ... The other case is still open. They ask for an analysis under other preferences. ... the understanding about the recursive construction, comparison procedures, and canonical forms is an open field.
